question: Should OpenClaw accept experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics as a core Doctor capability while the underlying MCP ownership stack is still unmerged?
rationale: The patch introduces a broad ownership and diagnostics model in core rather than repairing an established behavior, and the protected maintainer label indicates that implementation quality alone cannot settle the product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics direction
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated core Doctor surface, require the WAL-safe detector repair and real runtime proof, then continue reviewing the stack.

options.title: Keep diagnostics outside core for now
options.body: Pause this stacked core slice until the RFC or an external plugin/ClawHub-oriented design establishes the supported ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core diagnostics direction
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated core Doctor surface, require the WAL-safe detector repair and real runtime proof, then continue reviewing the stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct involvement on a protected maintainer-labeled feature, though the available history does not establish a definitive code owner.
